title: VelclawHost
summary: Understand the VelclawHost integration boundary for runtime, deployment, DNS, routing, TLS, and health evidence.

sections.heading: What VelclawHost does
body: Velclaw integrates VelclawHost as a hosting provider adapter. The application can select velclawhost alongside render and self-hosted providers.
The hosting adapter reads the VelclawHost API URL and API token from server-side environment configuration; credentials are not part of the public documentation payload.

sections.heading: Deployment boundary
body: Deployment requests are normalized before they reach a hosting provider. This keeps the product workflow independent from the provider-specific API contract.
VelclawHost should be treated as the runtime and control-plane boundary for deployment, domain, routing, TLS, and health state rather than as a second application workflow.

sections.heading: Observe independent states
body: A deployment record and a reachable page are different pieces of evidence. Runtime health, deployment status, domain routing, and certificate state should be observed independently.
This distinction prevents a successful build or an HTTP response from being treated as proof that every production control-plane step is complete.

sections.heading: Server-side configuration
body: Configure the provider only in the server environment that owns the deployment adapter. Never place provider tokens in static docs, browser bundles, or client-side configuration.
If the provider is unavailable, fall back to the configured hosting provider rather than assuming that a domain or deployment is live.
